questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code protects the database from many concurrent lookups for the same user? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
200 requests for the same uncached user arrive at the same moment and the database call succeeds. How many times is the SQL query executed?
choices: 200, since each request checks the cache before any value is stored
Once, because concurrent callers with the same key share a single in-flight call
Once per CPU core, since singleflight groups calls per goroutine scheduler
Twice: once by the first caller and once more by the callers that missed the cache

questions.prompt: Why does load check the cache again before calling the store?
choices: go-cache can return stale values, so a second read is needed for correctness
A caller can miss the cache just before another flight finishes and stores the value, then start a new flight; the re-check avoids a redundant query
To refresh the TTL of the existing entry
Because singleflight clears the cache entry when a flight starts

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the random jitter added to positiveTTL when storing a permission set?
choices: To make entries for different users expire at spread-out times so refreshes do not all hit the database together
To make a single user's entry live a little longer than the negative entry
To prevent two users from sharing the same cache key
To let Invalidate remove entries without calling Forget
